purpose: Authored illustrative case study; not customer data, not a held-out benchmark; references frozen before inference.

examples.text: The Ray-Ban Meta camera makes the glasses too heavy for my daily walk.

labels.rationale: Only the weight of the smart-glasses product is criticised.
evidence_quotes: The Ray-Ban Meta camera makes the glasses too heavy for my daily walk.

examples.text: I dislike the recording indicator on Ray-Ban Meta because strangers may miss it.

labels.rationale: Concern concerns the recording feature, with no wider-brand judgement.
evidence_quotes: I dislike the recording indicator on Ray-Ban Meta because strangers may miss it.

examples.text: I will not buy Ray-Ban Meta glasses: the battery life is too short for my commute.

labels.rationale: Purchase rejection concerns the smart-glasses product alone.
evidence_quotes: I will not buy Ray-Ban Meta glasses: the battery life is too short for my commute.

examples.text: Ray-Ban is responsible for the uncomfortable fit of these Meta smart glasses.

labels.rationale: Explicit manufacturer responsibility for product fit does not reject traditional eyewear.
evidence_quotes: Ray-Ban is responsible for the uncomfortable fit of these Meta smart glasses.

examples.text: Meta is responsible for how my voice requests are handled, and I distrust Meta with those recordings.

labels.rationale: The named target and responsible actor are Meta only.
evidence_quotes: Meta is responsible for how my voice requests are handled, and I distrust Meta with those recordings.

examples.text: I blame Meta, not Ray-Ban, for the unclear explanation of human review of AI recordings.

labels.rationale: Negation explicitly excludes Ray-Ban from responsibility.
evidence_quotes: I blame Meta, not Ray-Ban, for the unclear explanation of human review of AI recordings.

examples.text: Meta should fix its confusing AI privacy controls; Meta is responsible for explaining them.

labels.rationale: Criticism and responsibility focus on Meta controls, not the wider eyewear brand.
evidence_quotes: Meta should fix its confusing AI privacy controls; Meta is responsible for explaining them.

examples.text: Because of the smart-glasses privacy controversy, I won't buy any Ray-Ban sunglasses again.

labels.rationale: Direct causal rejection of traditional Ray-Ban purchases follows the controversy.
evidence_quotes: Because of the smart-glasses privacy controversy, I won't buy any Ray-Ban sunglasses again.

examples.text: After the Meta recording controversy, I distrust Ray-Ban's entire brand.

labels.rationale: Wider-brand distrust is expressly connected to the recording controversy.
evidence_quotes: After the Meta recording controversy, I distrust Ray-Ban's entire brand.

examples.text: I will avoid traditional Ray-Ban frames because the smart-glasses privacy scandal destroyed my confidence.

labels.rationale: The speaker directly links avoiding traditional frames to privacy controversy.
evidence_quotes: I will avoid traditional Ray-Ban frames because the smart-glasses privacy scandal destroyed my confidence.

examples.text: I will boycott Ray-Ban, including its ordinary sunglasses, due to the smart-glasses surveillance controversy.

labels.rationale: An explicit wider-brand boycott is causally connected to surveillance concerns.
evidence_quotes: I will boycott Ray-Ban, including its ordinary sunglasses, due to the smart-glasses surveillance controversy.

examples.text: Since the camera privacy controversy, I will stop buying Ray-Ban sunglasses.

labels.rationale: An explicit rejection of ordinary sunglasses is linked to the camera controversy.
evidence_quotes: Since the camera privacy controversy, I will stop buying Ray-Ban sunglasses.

examples.text: The smart-glasses privacy debate bothers me. The wider Ray-Ban brand seems less attractive lately.

labels.rationale: Product concern and diminished wider-brand appeal coexist without an explicit causal rejection.
evidence_quotes: The smart-glasses privacy debate bothers me. The wider Ray-Ban brand seems less attractive lately.

examples.text: I worry about recording by smart glasses. Looking at traditional Ray-Ban displays feels less pleasant now.

labels.rationale: A negative traditional-brand association accompanies recording concerns without a direct causal assertion.
evidence_quotes: I worry about recording by smart glasses. Looking at traditional Ray-Ban displays feels less pleasant now.

examples.text: The Meta glasses controversy is unsettling. Ray-Ban's overall image feels colder to me lately.

labels.rationale: The wider-brand image is negative alongside controversy, without an express causal claim.
evidence_quotes: The Meta glasses controversy is unsettling. Ray-Ban's overall image feels colder to me lately.

examples.text: My traditional Ray-Ban aviators still look elegant after years of use.

labels.rationale: The speaker praises ordinary eyewear without a purchase intention.
evidence_quotes: My traditional Ray-Ban aviators still look elegant after years of use.

examples.text: I plan to buy ordinary Ray-Ban sunglasses for their classic styling.

labels.rationale: A positive purchase intention concerns traditional eyewear.
evidence_quotes: I plan to buy ordinary Ray-Ban sunglasses for their classic styling.

examples.text: Traditional Ray-Ban frames remain excellent; I do not distrust the wider Ray-Ban brand because of smart glasses.

labels.rationale: The speaker explicitly negates wider-brand distrust.
evidence_quotes: Traditional Ray-Ban frames remain excellent; I do not distrust the wider Ray-Ban brand because of smart glasses.

examples.text: I love the Ray-Ban Meta speakers but dislike the camera pointing at people on the train.

labels.rationale: Mixed product sentiment contains no wider-brand rejection.
evidence_quotes: I love the Ray-Ban Meta speakers but dislike the camera pointing at people on the train.

examples.text: Ray-Ban Meta recording makes me nervous, but my ordinary Ray-Ban sunglasses are still wonderful.

labels.rationale: Traditional-brand praise is preserved alongside product criticism.
evidence_quotes: Ray-Ban Meta recording makes me nervous, but my ordinary Ray-Ban sunglasses are still wonderful.

examples.text: After reading that story, I am disappointed in them, whoever is actually responsible.

labels.rationale: Neither the story nor the actor is specified.
evidence_quotes: After reading that story, I am disappointed in them, whoever is actually responsible.

examples.text: Wonderful, another camera following everyone. Exactly what we all needed, obviously.

labels.rationale: Sarcasm suggests criticism but identifies no particular brand.
evidence_quotes: Wonderful, another camera following everyone. Exactly what we all needed, obviously.

examples.text: Do Ray-Ban Meta glasses notify people before recording, and where can I read the instructions?

labels.rationale: An information request does not assert negative sentiment or brand spillover.
evidence_quotes: Do Ray-Ban Meta glasses notify people before recording, and where can I read the instructions?

examples.text: Meta and Ray-Ban are both responsible for explaining this recording feature clearly; I like the glasses but find the instructions confusing.

labels.rationale: Shared responsibility is explicitly stated for product instructions, not wider-brand damage.
evidence_quotes: Meta and Ray-Ban are both responsible for explaining this recording feature clearly; I like the glasses but find the instructions confusing.
